templates.title: Velocity from acceleration; displacement and total distance

variants.problem:
A particle moves along a line with acceleration $a(t)=6 t - 6$ m/s² and initial velocity $v(0)=-24$ m/s.

(a) Find $v(t)$.
(b) Find the displacement and the total distance traveled for $0\le t\le6$.
variants.answer: $v(t)=3 t^{2} - 6 t - 24$; displacement $-36$ m; distance $124$ m
variants.solution:
(a) $v(t)=\int a\,dt=3 t^{2} - 6 t+C$, and $v(0)=-24$ gives $C=-24$: $v(t)=3 t^{2} - 6 t - 24=3 \left(t - 4\right) \left(t + 2\right)$.

(b) Displacement: $\int_0^{6}v\,dt=-36$ m.

$v$ changes sign at $t=4$ (negative before, positive after), so split the distance there:

\[\int_0^{6}|v|\,dt=-\int_0^{4}v\,dt+\int_{4}^{6}v\,dt=80+44=124\ \text{m}.\]

(a) Find $v(t)$.
(b) Find the displacement and the total distance traveled for $0\le t\le3$.
variants.solution:
(a) $v(t)=\int a\,dt=t^{2}+C$, and $v(0)=-1$ gives $C=-1$: $v(t)=t^{2} - 1=\left(t - 1\right) \left(t + 1\right)$.

$v$ changes sign at $t=1$ (negative before, positive after), so split the distance there:

\[\int_0^{3}|v|\,dt=-\int_0^{1}v\,dt+\int_{1}^{3}v\,dt=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{20}{3}=\frac{22}{3}\ \text{m}.\]

templates.title: Area between a parabola and a line

variants.problem: Find the area of the region enclosed by $y=- 3 x^{2} + 15 x - 10$ and $y=3 x - 1$.
variants.solution:
The curves meet where $- 3 x^{2} + 15 x - 10=3 x - 1$, i.e. $3 x^{2} - 12 x + 9=0$, so $x=1$ and $x=3$. Between them the parabola is on top (test $x=2$, for example).

\[A=\int_{1}^{3}\left[\left(- 3 x^{2} + 15 x - 10\right)-\left(3 x - 1\right)\right]dx=\int_{1}^{3}\left(- 3 x^{2} + 12 x - 9\right)dx=\left[- x^{3} + 6 x^{2} - 9 x\right]_{1}^{3}=4.\]

variants.problem: Find the area of the region enclosed by $y=- 3 x^{2} + 12 x - 19$ and $y=- 3 x - 1$.
variants.solution:
The curves meet where $- 3 x^{2} + 12 x - 19=- 3 x - 1$, i.e. $3 x^{2} - 15 x + 18=0$, so $x=2$ and $x=3$. Between them the parabola is on top (test $x=\frac{5}{2}$, for example).

\[A=\int_{2}^{3}\left[\left(- 3 x^{2} + 12 x - 19\right)-\left(- 3 x - 1\right)\right]dx=\int_{2}^{3}\left(- 3 x^{2} + 15 x - 18\right)dx=\left[- x^{3} + \frac{15 x^{2}}{2} - 18 x\right]_{2}^{3}=\frac{1}{2}.\]

\[A=\int_{-3}^{2}\left[\left(- 3 x^{2} - x + 17\right)-\left(2 x - 1\right)\right]dx=\int_{-3}^{2}\left(- 3 x^{2} - 3 x + 18\right)dx=\left[- x^{3} - \frac{3 x^{2}}{2} + 18 x\right]_{-3}^{2}=\frac{125}{2}.\]

variants.problem: Find the area of the region enclosed by $y=- x^{2} - 6 x - 6$ and $y=- 3 x - 4$.

\[A=\int_{-2}^{-1}\left[\left(- x^{2} - 6 x - 6\right)-\left(- 3 x - 4\right)\right]dx=\int_{-2}^{-1}\left(- x^{2} - 3 x - 2\right)dx=\left[- \frac{x^{3}}{3} - \frac{3 x^{2}}{2} - 2 x\right]_{-2}^{-1}=\frac{1}{6}.\]

\[A=\int_{2}^{4}\left[\left(- 3 x^{2} + 21 x - 24\right)-\left(3 x\right)\right]dx=\int_{2}^{4}\left(- 3 x^{2} + 18 x - 24\right)dx=\left[- x^{3} + 9 x^{2} - 24 x\right]_{2}^{4}=4.\]

variants.problem: Find the area of the region enclosed by $y=- x^{2} - 2 x + 2$ and $y=- 3 x$.
variants.solution:
The curves meet where $- x^{2} - 2 x + 2=- 3 x$, i.e. $x^{2} - x - 2=0$, so $x=-1$ and $x=2$. Between them the parabola is on top (test $x=\frac{1}{2}$, for example).

\[A=\int_{-1}^{2}\left[\left(- x^{2} - 2 x + 2\right)-\left(- 3 x\right)\right]dx=\int_{-1}^{2}\left(- x^{2} + x + 2\right)dx=\left[- \frac{x^{3}}{3} + \frac{x^{2}}{2} + 2 x\right]_{-1}^{2}=\frac{9}{2}.\]

variants.problem: Find the area of the region enclosed by $y=- 3 x^{2} + 11 x - 5$ and $y=2 x + 1$.

\[A=\int_{1}^{2}\left[\left(- 3 x^{2} + 11 x - 5\right)-\left(2 x + 1\right)\right]dx=\int_{1}^{2}\left(- 3 x^{2} + 9 x - 6\right)dx=\left[- x^{3} + \frac{9 x^{2}}{2} - 6 x\right]_{1}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}.\]

variants.problem: Find the area of the region enclosed by $y=- 2 x^{2} + 3 x + 2$ and $y=3 x$.

\[A=\int_{-1}^{1}\left[\left(- 2 x^{2} + 3 x + 2\right)-\left(3 x\right)\right]dx=\int_{-1}^{1}\left(2 - 2 x^{2}\right)dx=\left[- \frac{2 x^{3}}{3} + 2 x\right]_{-1}^{1}=\frac{8}{3}.\]

variants.problem: An object at $102$°C is placed in a room kept at $22$°C. After $10$ minutes its temperature is $\frac{226}{3}$°C. By Newton's law of cooling, $T'=-k(T-22)$. When will the object be at $38$°C?
variants.solution:
The solution of $T'=-k(T-22)$ is $T(t)=22+(T_0-22)e^{-kt}=22+(80)e^{-kt}$.

Use the measurement: $\frac{226}{3}=22+(80)e^{-10k}$, so $e^{-10k}=\frac{2}{3}$ and $k=\dfrac{\ln\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}{10}\approx0.04055$ per minute.

Now solve $38=22+(80)e^{-kt}$: $e^{-kt}=\frac{1}{5}$, so

\[t=\frac{\ln 5}{k}=10\cdot\frac{\ln 5}{\ln\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}\approx39.69\ \text{minutes}.\]

variants.problem:

\[\frac{dy}{dx}=x \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}\,y,\qquad y(0)=-2.\]
variants.solution:
Separate the variables and integrate both sides:

\[\frac{dy}{y}=x \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}\,dx\ \Rightarrow\ \ln|y|=\frac{\sin{\left(x^{2} \right)}}{2}+C\ \Rightarrow\ y=Ae^{\frac{\sin{\left(x^{2} \right)}}{2}}.\]

$y(0)=-2$ gives $A=-2$:

\[y=- 2 e^{\frac{\sin{\left(x^{2} \right)}}{2}}.\]

templates.title: Does the improper integral converge? If so, evaluate it

variants.problem:
Determine whether the integral converges or diverges, and evaluate it if it converges:

\[\int_{1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{x^{2}}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Write it as a limit of proper integrals:

\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\int_1^T\frac{1}{x^{2}}\,dx=\lim_{T\to\infty}\left(\frac{T - 1}{T}\right)=1.\]

The limit is finite, so the integral converges to $1$.

\[\lim_{T\to0^+}\int_T^1\frac{3}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\,dx=\lim_{T\to0^+}\left(\frac{9}{2} - \frac{9 T^{\frac{2}{3}}}{2}\right)=\frac{9}{2}.\]

The limit is finite, so the integral converges to $\frac{9}{2}$.

\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\int_0^T2 x e^{- \frac{x}{2}}\,dx=\lim_{T\to\infty}\left(4 \left(- T + 2 e^{\frac{T}{2}} - 2\right) e^{- \frac{T}{2}}\right)\quad\text{(by parts)}=8.\]

The limit is finite, so the integral converges to $8$.

\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\int_0^T2 x e^{- 3 x}\,dx=\lim_{T\to\infty}\left(\frac{2 \left(- 3 T + e^{3 T} - 1\right) e^{- 3 T}}{9}\right)\quad\text{(by parts)}=\frac{2}{9}.\]

The limit is finite, so the integral converges to $\frac{2}{9}$.

variants.problem:
Determine whether the integral converges or diverges, and evaluate it if it converges:

\[\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{2}{x^{2} + 1}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Write it as a limit of proper integrals:

\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\int_{0}^T\frac{2}{x^{2} + 1}\,dx=\lim_{T\to\infty}\left(2 \operatorname{atan}{\left(T \right)}\right)=\pi.\]

The limit is finite, so the integral converges to $\pi$.

variants.problem:
Determine whether the integral converges or diverges, and evaluate it if it converges:

\[\int_{1}^{\infty}\frac{3}{x^{3}}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Write it as a limit of proper integrals:

\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\int_1^T\frac{3}{x^{3}}\,dx=\lim_{T\to\infty}\left(\frac{3}{2} - \frac{3}{2 T^{2}}\right)=\frac{3}{2}.\]

The limit is finite, so the integral converges to $\frac{3}{2}$.

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x^{5} \ln{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=\ln{\left(x \right)}$ and $dv=x^{5}\,dx$, so $du=\frac{1}{x}\,dx$ and $v=\frac{x^{6}}{6}$:

\[\int x^{5} \ln{\left(x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{6} \ln{\left(x \right)}}{6}-\int \frac{x^{5}}{6}\,dx.\]

The last integral is $\int \frac{x^{5}}{6}\,dx=\frac{x^{6}}{36}$.

So

\[\int x^{5} \ln{\left(x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{6} \left(6 \ln{\left(x \right)} - 1\right)}{36}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x \sin{\left(5 x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x$ and $dv=\sin{\left(5 x \right)}\,dx$, so $du=1\,dx$ and $v=- \frac{\cos{\left(5 x \right)}}{5}$:

\[\int x \sin{\left(5 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x \cos{\left(5 x \right)}}{5}-\int - \frac{\cos{\left(5 x \right)}}{5}\,dx.\]

The last integral is $\int - \frac{\cos{\left(5 x \right)}}{5}\,dx=- \frac{\sin{\left(5 x \right)}}{25}$.

So

\[\int x \sin{\left(5 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x \cos{\left(5 x \right)}}{5} + \frac{\sin{\left(5 x \right)}}{25}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=\sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=- \cos{\left(x \right)}$:

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- x^{2} \cos{\left(x \right)}-\int - 2 x \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=- 2 \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=- 2 \sin{\left(x \right)}$):

\[\int - 2 x \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- 2 x \sin{\left(x \right)}-\int - 2 \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- 2 x \sin{\left(x \right)} - 2 \cos{\left(x \right)}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- x^{2} \cos{\left(x \right)} + 2 x \sin{\left(x \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(x \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x^{2} e^{4 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=e^{4 x}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=\frac{e^{4 x}}{4}$:

\[\int x^{2} e^{4 x}\,dx=\frac{x^{2} e^{4 x}}{4}-\int \frac{x e^{4 x}}{2}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=\frac{e^{4 x}}{2}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=\frac{e^{4 x}}{8}$):

\[\int \frac{x e^{4 x}}{2}\,dx=\frac{x e^{4 x}}{8}-\int \frac{e^{4 x}}{8}\,dx=\frac{\left(4 x - 1\right) e^{4 x}}{32}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} e^{4 x}\,dx=\frac{\left(8 x^{2} - 4 x + 1\right) e^{4 x}}{32}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=\cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=\frac{\sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}$:

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{2} \sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}-\int x \sin{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=\sin{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=- \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}$):

\[\int x \sin{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x \cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}-\int - \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}\,dx=- \frac{x \cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2} + \frac{\sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{4}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{2} \sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2} + \frac{x \cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2} - \frac{\sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{4}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x^{2} e^{2 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=e^{2 x}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=\frac{e^{2 x}}{2}$:

\[\int x^{2} e^{2 x}\,dx=\frac{x^{2} e^{2 x}}{2}-\int x e^{2 x}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=e^{2 x}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=\frac{e^{2 x}}{2}$):

\[\int x e^{2 x}\,dx=\frac{x e^{2 x}}{2}-\int \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}\,dx=\frac{\left(2 x - 1\right) e^{2 x}}{4}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} e^{2 x}\,dx=\frac{\left(2 x^{2} - 2 x + 1\right) e^{2 x}}{4}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x e^{- 3 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x$ and $dv=e^{- 3 x}\,dx$, so $du=1\,dx$ and $v=- \frac{e^{- 3 x}}{3}$:

\[\int x e^{- 3 x}\,dx=- \frac{x e^{- 3 x}}{3}-\int - \frac{e^{- 3 x}}{3}\,dx.\]

The last integral is $\int - \frac{e^{- 3 x}}{3}\,dx=\frac{e^{- 3 x}}{9}$.

So

\[\int x e^{- 3 x}\,dx=\frac{\left(- 3 x - 1\right) e^{- 3 x}}{9}+C.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=\cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=\sin{\left(x \right)}$:

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx=x^{2} \sin{\left(x \right)}-\int 2 x \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=2 \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=- 2 \cos{\left(x \right)}$):

\[\int 2 x \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- 2 x \cos{\left(x \right)}-\int - 2 \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- 2 x \cos{\left(x \right)} + 2 \sin{\left(x \right)}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx=x^{2} \sin{\left(x \right)} + 2 x \cos{\left(x \right)} - 2 \sin{\left(x \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=\frac{2 e^{5 x}}{5}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=\frac{2 e^{5 x}}{25}$):

\[\int \frac{2 x e^{5 x}}{5}\,dx=\frac{2 x e^{5 x}}{25}-\int \frac{2 e^{5 x}}{25}\,dx=\frac{\left(10 x - 2\right) e^{5 x}}{125}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} e^{5 x}\,dx=\frac{\left(25 x^{2} - 10 x + 2\right) e^{5 x}}{125}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \ln{\left(x \right)}^{2}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=\ln{\left(x \right)}^{2}$ and $dv=1\,dx$, so $du=\frac{2 \ln{\left(x \right)}}{x}\,dx$ and $v=x$:

\[\int \ln{\left(x \right)}^{2}\,dx=x \ln{\left(x \right)}^{2}-\int 2 \ln{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=\ln{\left(x \right)}$, $dv=2\,dx$ (so $du=\frac{1}{x}\,dx$, $v=2 x$):

\[\int 2 \ln{\left(x \right)}\,dx=2 x \ln{\left(x \right)}-\int 2\,dx=2 x \ln{\left(x \right)} - 2 x.\]

So

\[\int \ln{\left(x \right)}^{2}\,dx=x \left(\ln{\left(x \right)}^{2} - 2 \ln{\left(x \right)} + 2\right)+C.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(3 x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=\cos{\left(3 x \right)}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=\frac{\sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}$:

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(3 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{2} \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}-\int \frac{2 x \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=\frac{2 \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=- \frac{2 \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{9}$):

\[\int \frac{2 x \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}\,dx=- \frac{2 x \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{9}-\int - \frac{2 \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{9}\,dx=- \frac{2 x \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{9} + \frac{2 \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{27}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(3 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{2} \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{3} + \frac{2 x \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{9} - \frac{2 \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{27}+C.\]

variants.problem:

So

variants.problem:

The last integral is $\int \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}\,dx=\frac{e^{2 x}}{4}$.

So

\[\int x e^{2 x}\,dx=\frac{\left(2 x - 1\right) e^{2 x}}{4}+C.\]

variants.problem:

So

variants.problem:

The last integral is $\int \frac{\sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}\,dx=- \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{4}$.

So

\[\int x \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x \sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2} + \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{4}+C.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int x^{2} \cos{\left(4 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{2} \sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{4}-\int \frac{x \sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=\frac{\sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=- \frac{\cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{8}$):

\[\int \frac{x \sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\,dx=- \frac{x \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{8}-\int - \frac{\cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{8}\,dx=- \frac{x \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{8} + \frac{\sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{32}.\]

So

variants.problem:

The last integral is $\int \frac{x^{2}}{3}\,dx=\frac{x^{3}}{9}$.

So

\[\int x^{2} \ln{\left(x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{3} \left(3 \ln{\left(x \right)} - 1\right)}{9}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x e^{x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x$ and $dv=e^{x}\,dx$, so $du=1\,dx$ and $v=e^{x}$:

\[\int x e^{x}\,dx=x e^{x}-\int e^{x}\,dx.\]

The last integral is $\int e^{x}\,dx=e^{x}$.

So

\[\int x e^{x}\,dx=\left(x - 1\right) e^{x}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]

Take $u=x$ and $dv=\cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx$, so $du=1\,dx$ and $v=\sin{\left(x \right)}$:

\[\int x \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx=x \sin{\left(x \right)}-\int \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]

The last integral is $\int \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- \cos{\left(x \right)}$.

So

\[\int x \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx=x \sin{\left(x \right)} + \cos{\left(x \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x^{2} e^{x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=e^{x}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=e^{x}$:

\[\int x^{2} e^{x}\,dx=x^{2} e^{x}-\int 2 x e^{x}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=2 e^{x}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=2 e^{x}$):

\[\int 2 x e^{x}\,dx=2 x e^{x}-\int 2 e^{x}\,dx=\left(2 x - 2\right) e^{x}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} e^{x}\,dx=\left(x^{2} - 2 x + 2\right) e^{x}+C.\]

variants.problem:

The last integral is $\int - \frac{e^{- 4 x}}{4}\,dx=\frac{e^{- 4 x}}{16}$.

So

\[\int x e^{- 4 x}\,dx=\frac{\left(- 4 x - 1\right) e^{- 4 x}}{16}+C.\]

variants.problem:

The last integral is $\int \frac{x}{2}\,dx=\frac{x^{2}}{4}$.

So

\[\int x \ln{\left(x \right)}\,dx=\frac{x^{2} \left(2 \ln{\left(x \right)} - 1\right)}{4}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x e^{- x}\,dx.\]

Take $u=x$ and $dv=e^{- x}\,dx$, so $du=1\,dx$ and $v=- e^{- x}$:

\[\int x e^{- x}\,dx=- x e^{- x}-\int - e^{- x}\,dx.\]

The last integral is $\int - e^{- x}\,dx=e^{- x}$.

So

\[\int x e^{- x}\,dx=\left(- x - 1\right) e^{- x}+C.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(3 x \right)}\,dx.\]

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(3 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x^{2} \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}-\int - \frac{2 x \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=- \frac{2 \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=- \frac{2 \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{9}$):

\[\int - \frac{2 x \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}\,dx=- \frac{2 x \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{9}-\int - \frac{2 \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{9}\,dx=- \frac{2 x \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{9} - \frac{2 \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{27}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(3 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x^{2} \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{3} + \frac{2 x \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{9} + \frac{2 \cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{27}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x e^{5 x}\,dx.\]

Take $u=x$ and $dv=e^{5 x}\,dx$, so $du=1\,dx$ and $v=\frac{e^{5 x}}{5}$:

The last integral is $\int \frac{e^{5 x}}{5}\,dx=\frac{e^{5 x}}{25}$.

So

\[\int x e^{5 x}\,dx=\frac{\left(5 x - 1\right) e^{5 x}}{25}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x^{4} \ln{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]

So

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=\sin{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=- \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}$:

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x^{2} \cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}-\int - x \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=- \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=- \frac{\sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}$):

\[\int - x \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x \sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}-\int - \frac{\sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}\,dx=- \frac{x \sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2} - \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{4}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x^{2} \cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2} + \frac{x \sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2} + \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{4}+C.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int x \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]

The last integral is $\int - \cos{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- \sin{\left(x \right)}$.

So

\[\int x \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- x \cos{\left(x \right)} + \sin{\left(x \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:

variants.problem:
Evaluate

variants.solution:
Take $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=\sin{\left(4 x \right)}\,dx$, so $du=2 x\,dx$ and $v=- \frac{\cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{4}$:

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(4 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x^{2} \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{4}-\int - \frac{x \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\,dx.\]

Use parts again on the last integral, with $u=x$, $dv=- \frac{\cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\,dx$ (so $du=1\,dx$, $v=- \frac{\sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{8}$):

\[\int - \frac{x \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\,dx=- \frac{x \sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{8}-\int - \frac{\sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{8}\,dx=- \frac{x \sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{8} - \frac{\cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{32}.\]

So

\[\int x^{2} \sin{\left(4 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{x^{2} \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{4} + \frac{x \sin{\left(4 x \right)}}{8} + \frac{\cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{32}+C.\]

templates.title: A salt-mixing tank with constant volume

variants.problem:
A tank holds $50$ L of brine containing $10$ g of salt. Brine with $5$ g/L of salt flows in at $5$ L/min, and the well-mixed solution flows out at the same rate.

(a) Find the amount of salt $y(t)$ after $t$ minutes.
(b) How much salt is there after $10$ minutes, and in the long run?
variants.solution:
(a) Salt in: $5\cdot5=25$ g/min. Salt out: $5\cdot\frac{y}{50}$ g/min. So

\[\frac{dy}{dt}=25-\frac{5}{50}y=-\frac{1}{10}\left(y-250\right),\qquad y(0)=10.\]

So $y-250$ decays exponentially: $y-250=(-240)e^{-\frac{1}{10}t}$, i.e. $y(t)=250 - 240 e^{- \frac{t}{10}}$.

(b) $y(10)=250 - \frac{240}{e}\approx161.71$ g. As $t\to\infty$ the exponential dies out, so $y\to250$ g.

templates.title: Riemann sum approximation of an area

variants.problem:
Let $R$ be the region under $y=8 - x$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le8$.

(a) Write the area of $R$ as an integral and evaluate it.
(b) Approximate the area with $n=4$ rectangles using right endpoints.
variants.solution:
(a) $\displaystyle A=\int_{0}^{8}\left(8 - x\right)dx=\left[- \frac{x^{2}}{2} + 8 x\right]_{0}^{8}=32$.

(b) $\Delta x=\frac{8-0}{4}=2$, and the sample points (right endpoints) are $2$, $4$, $6$, $8$:

\[2\left[f\left(2\right)+f\left(4\right)+f\left(6\right)+f\left(8\right)\right]=2\left[6+4+2+0\right]=24.\]

templates.title: Lifting a bucket with a heavy cable

variants.problem:
A cable that weighs $3$ lb per foot lifts a bucket of water weighing $20$ lb from the bottom of a well $10$ ft deep to the top.

(a) How much work is done?
(b) How far above the bottom of the well is the bucket when exactly half of that work has been done?
variants.solution:
Let $s$ be how far the bucket has risen. The force needed then is the bucket plus the $10-s$ ft of cable still hanging: $F(s)=20+3(10-s)$ lb.

(b) The work done raising it the first $s$ feet is $\int_0^s F=- \frac{3 s^{2}}{2} + 50 s$. Set this equal to $\frac{350}2$:

\[- \frac{3 s^{2}}{2} + 50 s=175.\]

Only one root of this quadratic lies in $[0,10]$: $s=\frac{50}{3} - \frac{5 \sqrt{58}}{3}\approx3.974$ ft above the bottom.

\[\frac{3 x^{2} - 3 x + 3}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x + 1} + \frac{C}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=\frac{39}{10}$, $x=-1$ gives $B=- \frac{3}{2}$, $x=2$ gives $C=\frac{3}{5}$. So

\[\frac{3 x^{2} - 3 x + 3}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}=\frac{39}{10 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{3}{2 \left(x + 1\right)} + \frac{3}{5 \left(x - 2\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 x^{2} - 3 x + 3}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}\,dx=\frac{3 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{5} - \frac{3 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{2} + \frac{39 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{10}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 4 x + 12=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{2 - 2 x^{2}}{x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 4 x + 12}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x - 2} + \frac{C}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=- \frac{3}{10}$, $x=2$ gives $B=\frac{3}{2}$, $x=3$ gives $C=- \frac{16}{5}$. So

\[\frac{2 - 2 x^{2}}{x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 4 x + 12}=- \frac{3}{10 \left(x + 2\right)} + \frac{3}{2 \left(x - 2\right)} - \frac{16}{5 \left(x - 3\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{2 - 2 x^{2}}{x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 4 x + 12}\,dx=- \frac{16 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{5} + \frac{3 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{2} - \frac{3 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}}{10}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - x - 3=\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{2 - x^{2}}{x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - x - 3}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x + 1} + \frac{C}{x - 1}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=- \frac{7}{8}$, $x=-1$ gives $B=- \frac{1}{4}$, $x=1$ gives $C=\frac{1}{8}$. So

\[\frac{2 - x^{2}}{x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - x - 3}=- \frac{7}{8 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{1}{4 \left(x + 1\right)} + \frac{1}{8 \left(x - 1\right)}.\]

\[\int \frac{2 - x^{2}}{x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - x - 3}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)}}{8} - \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{4} - \frac{7 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{8}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} - x^{2} - 4 x + 4=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- x^{2} + x - 2}{x^{3} - x^{2} - 4 x + 4}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x - 1} + \frac{C}{x - 2}.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{4 x - 2}{x^{2} - 9}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 9=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{4 x - 2}{x^{2} - 9}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=\frac{7}{3}$, $x=3$ gives $B=\frac{5}{3}$. So

\[\frac{4 x - 2}{x^{2} - 9}=\frac{7}{3 \left(x + 3\right)} + \frac{5}{3 \left(x - 3\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{4 x - 2}{x^{2} - 9}\,dx=\frac{5 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{3} + \frac{7 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{3}+C.\]

\[\int \frac{4 x + 2}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 5 x + 6=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{4 x + 2}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}=\frac{A}{x - 2} + \frac{B}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=2$ gives $A=-10$, $x=3$ gives $B=14$. So

\[\frac{4 x + 2}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}=- \frac{10}{x - 2} + \frac{14}{x - 3}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{4 x + 2}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}\,dx=14 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)} - 10 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{x - 1}{x^{2} + x - 6}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} + x - 6=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{x - 1}{x^{2} + x - 6}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=\frac{4}{5}$, $x=2$ gives $B=\frac{1}{5}$. So

\[\frac{x - 1}{x^{2} + x - 6}=\frac{4}{5 \left(x + 3\right)} + \frac{1}{5 \left(x - 2\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{x - 1}{x^{2} + x - 6}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{5} + \frac{4 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{5}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 6 x=x \left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- x^{2} + 3 x - 4}{x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 6 x}=\frac{A}{x} + \frac{B}{x - 2} + \frac{C}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=0$ gives $A=- \frac{2}{3}$, $x=2$ gives $B=1$, $x=3$ gives $C=- \frac{4}{3}$. So

\[\frac{- x^{2} + 3 x - 4}{x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 6 x}=\frac{1}{x - 2} - \frac{4}{3 \left(x - 3\right)} - \frac{2}{3 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- x^{2} + 3 x - 4}{x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 6 x}\,dx=- \frac{2 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{3} - \frac{4 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{3} + \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}+C.\]

\[\int - \frac{1}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 5 x + 6=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 2\right)$. Write

\[- \frac{1}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}=\frac{A}{x - 2} + \frac{B}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=2$ gives $A=1$, $x=3$ gives $B=-1$. So

\[- \frac{1}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}=\frac{1}{x - 2} - \frac{1}{x - 3}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int - \frac{1}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}\,dx=- \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)} + \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{x^{2} + x - 3}{x^{3} - x^{2} - 6 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{3} - x^{2} - 6 x=x \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{x^{2} + x - 3}{x^{3} - x^{2} - 6 x}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x} + \frac{C}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=- \frac{1}{10}$, $x=0$ gives $B=\frac{1}{2}$, $x=3$ gives $C=\frac{3}{5}$. So

\[\frac{x^{2} + x - 3}{x^{3} - x^{2} - 6 x}=- \frac{1}{10 \left(x + 2\right)} + \frac{3}{5 \left(x - 3\right)} + \frac{1}{2 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{x^{2} + x - 3}{x^{3} - x^{2} - 6 x}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{2} + \frac{3 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{5} - \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}}{10}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + 4 x^{2} + 3 x=x \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{4 x^{2} - 2 x - 1}{x^{3} + 4 x^{2} + 3 x}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x + 1} + \frac{C}{x}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=\frac{41}{6}$, $x=-1$ gives $B=- \frac{5}{2}$, $x=0$ gives $C=- \frac{1}{3}$. So

\[\frac{4 x^{2} - 2 x - 1}{x^{3} + 4 x^{2} + 3 x}=\frac{41}{6 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{5}{2 \left(x + 1\right)} - \frac{1}{3 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{4 x^{2} - 2 x - 1}{x^{3} + 4 x^{2} + 3 x}\,dx=- \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{3} - \frac{5 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{2} + \frac{41 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{6}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x=x \left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{2 x^{2} - 4 x + 1}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x} + \frac{C}{x - 1}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=\frac{17}{6}$, $x=0$ gives $B=- \frac{1}{2}$, $x=1$ gives $C=- \frac{1}{3}$. So

\[\frac{2 x^{2} - 4 x + 1}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x}=\frac{17}{6 \left(x + 2\right)} - \frac{1}{3 \left(x - 1\right)} - \frac{1}{2 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{2 x^{2} - 4 x + 1}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x}\,dx=- \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{2} - \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)}}{3} + \frac{17 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}}{6}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- 3 x^{2} - x - 1}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x + 1} + \frac{C}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=- \frac{5}{2}$, $x=-1$ gives $B=\frac{1}{2}$, $x=2$ gives $C=-1$. So

\[\frac{- 3 x^{2} - x - 1}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}=- \frac{5}{2 \left(x + 3\right)} + \frac{1}{2 \left(x + 1\right)} - \frac{1}{x - 2}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- 3 x^{2} - x - 1}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}\,dx=- \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)} + \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{2} - \frac{5 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{2}+C.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=1$, $x=2$ gives $B=-1$. So

\[\int - \frac{4}{x^{2} - 4}\,dx=- \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)} + \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}+C.\]

\[\int - \frac{4 x}{x^{2} + 3 x + 2}\,dx.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=-8$, $x=-1$ gives $B=4$. So

\[- \frac{4 x}{x^{2} + 3 x + 2}=- \frac{8}{x + 2} + \frac{4}{x + 1}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int - \frac{4 x}{x^{2} + 3 x + 2}\,dx=4 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)} - 8 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int \frac{x^{2} - 2 x - 4}{x^{3} - 4 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{3} - 4 x=x \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{x^{2} - 2 x - 4}{x^{3} - 4 x}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x} + \frac{C}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=\frac{1}{2}$, $x=0$ gives $B=1$, $x=2$ gives $C=- \frac{1}{2}$. So

\[\frac{x^{2} - 2 x - 4}{x^{3} - 4 x}=\frac{1}{2 \left(x + 2\right)} - \frac{1}{2 \left(x - 2\right)} + \frac{1}{x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{x^{2} - 2 x - 4}{x^{3} - 4 x}\,dx=\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)} - \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{2} + \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}}{2}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 5 x + 6=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}=\frac{A}{x - 2} + \frac{B}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=2$ gives $A=1$, $x=3$ gives $B=-3$. So

\[\frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}=\frac{1}{x - 2} - \frac{3}{x - 3}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 5 x + 6}\,dx=- 3 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)} + \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{3 x - 1}{x^{2} - x - 2}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - x - 2=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)$. Write

\[\frac{3 x - 1}{x^{2} - x - 2}=\frac{A}{x + 1} + \frac{B}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-1$ gives $A=\frac{4}{3}$, $x=2$ gives $B=\frac{5}{3}$. So

\[\frac{3 x - 1}{x^{2} - x - 2}=\frac{4}{3 \left(x + 1\right)} + \frac{5}{3 \left(x - 2\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 x - 1}{x^{2} - x - 2}\,dx=\frac{5 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{3} + \frac{4 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{3}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{1}{x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 3 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 3 x=x \left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 1\right)$. Write

\[\frac{1}{x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 3 x}=\frac{A}{x} + \frac{B}{x - 1} + \frac{C}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=0$ gives $A=\frac{1}{3}$, $x=1$ gives $B=- \frac{1}{2}$, $x=3$ gives $C=\frac{1}{6}$. So

\[\frac{1}{x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 3 x}=- \frac{1}{2 \left(x - 1\right)} + \frac{1}{6 \left(x - 3\right)} + \frac{1}{3 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{1}{x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 3 x}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{3} + \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{6} - \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)}}{2}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 9 x - 18=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 2\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{x^{2} + 1}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 9 x - 18}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x + 2} + \frac{C}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=\frac{5}{3}$, $x=-2$ gives $B=-1$, $x=3$ gives $C=\frac{1}{3}$. So

\[\frac{x^{2} + 1}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 9 x - 18}=\frac{5}{3 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{1}{x + 2} + \frac{1}{3 \left(x - 3\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{x^{2} + 1}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 9 x - 18}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{3} - \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)} + \frac{5 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{3}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 3 x=x \left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- 4 x^{2} + 2 x - 3}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 3 x}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x} + \frac{C}{x - 1}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=- \frac{15}{4}$, $x=0$ gives $B=1$, $x=1$ gives $C=- \frac{5}{4}$. So

\[\frac{- 4 x^{2} + 2 x - 3}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 3 x}=- \frac{15}{4 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{5}{4 \left(x - 1\right)} + \frac{1}{x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- 4 x^{2} + 2 x - 3}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 3 x}\,dx=\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)} - \frac{5 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)}}{4} - \frac{15 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{4}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{3 - 3 x}{x^{2} - x - 2}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - x - 2=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)$. Write

\[\frac{3 - 3 x}{x^{2} - x - 2}=\frac{A}{x + 1} + \frac{B}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-1$ gives $A=-2$, $x=2$ gives $B=-1$. So

\[\frac{3 - 3 x}{x^{2} - x - 2}=- \frac{2}{x + 1} - \frac{1}{x - 2}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 - 3 x}{x^{2} - x - 2}\,dx=- \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)} - 2 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{- 4 x - 3}{x^{2} - 1}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 1=\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 1\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- 4 x - 3}{x^{2} - 1}=\frac{A}{x + 1} + \frac{B}{x - 1}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-1$ gives $A=- \frac{1}{2}$, $x=1$ gives $B=- \frac{7}{2}$. So

\[\frac{- 4 x - 3}{x^{2} - 1}=- \frac{1}{2 \left(x + 1\right)} - \frac{7}{2 \left(x - 1\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- 4 x - 3}{x^{2} - 1}\,dx=- \frac{7 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)}}{2} - \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{2}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 3 x + 2}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 3 x + 2=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x - 1\right)$. Write

\[\frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 3 x + 2}=\frac{A}{x - 1} + \frac{B}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=1$ gives $A=-1$, $x=2$ gives $B=-1$. So

\[\frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 3 x + 2}=- \frac{1}{x - 1} - \frac{1}{x - 2}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 3 x + 2}\,dx=- \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)} - \ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{1 - 3 x}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x=x \left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{1 - 3 x}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x} + \frac{C}{x - 1}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=\frac{7}{6}$, $x=0$ gives $B=- \frac{1}{2}$, $x=1$ gives $C=- \frac{2}{3}$. So

\[\frac{1 - 3 x}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x}=\frac{7}{6 \left(x + 2\right)} - \frac{2}{3 \left(x - 1\right)} - \frac{1}{2 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{1 - 3 x}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 2 x}\,dx=- \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{2} - \frac{2 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)}}{3} + \frac{7 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}}{6}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{x^{2} + 4}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x + 1} + \frac{C}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=2$, $x=-1$ gives $B=- \frac{5}{3}$, $x=2$ gives $C=\frac{2}{3}$. So

\[\frac{x^{2} + 4}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4}=\frac{2}{x + 2} - \frac{5}{3 \left(x + 1\right)} + \frac{2}{3 \left(x - 2\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{x^{2} + 4}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4}\,dx=\frac{2 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{3} - \frac{5 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{3} + 2 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{3 x + 4}{x^{2} + 3 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} + 3 x=x \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{3 x + 4}{x^{2} + 3 x}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=\frac{5}{3}$, $x=0$ gives $B=\frac{4}{3}$. So

\[\frac{3 x + 4}{x^{2} + 3 x}=\frac{5}{3 \left(x + 3\right)} + \frac{4}{3 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 x + 4}{x^{2} + 3 x}\,dx=\frac{4 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{3} + \frac{5 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{3}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- 3 x^{2} - x + 4}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x + 1} + \frac{C}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=-2$, $x=-1$ gives $B=- \frac{1}{3}$, $x=2$ gives $C=- \frac{2}{3}$. So

\[\frac{- 3 x^{2} - x + 4}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}=- \frac{2}{x + 3} - \frac{1}{3 \left(x + 1\right)} - \frac{2}{3 \left(x - 2\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- 3 x^{2} - x + 4}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 6}\,dx=- \frac{2 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{3} - \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{3} - 2 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{- x - 1}{x^{2} + 3 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} + 3 x=x \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- x - 1}{x^{2} + 3 x}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=- \frac{2}{3}$, $x=0$ gives $B=- \frac{1}{3}$. So

\[\frac{- x - 1}{x^{2} + 3 x}=- \frac{2}{3 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{1}{3 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- x - 1}{x^{2} + 3 x}\,dx=- \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{3} - \frac{2 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{3}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{- 3 x^{2} + 4 x - 1}{x^{3} - 9 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{3} - 9 x=x \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- 3 x^{2} + 4 x - 1}{x^{3} - 9 x}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x} + \frac{C}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=- \frac{20}{9}$, $x=0$ gives $B=\frac{1}{9}$, $x=3$ gives $C=- \frac{8}{9}$. So

\[\frac{- 3 x^{2} + 4 x - 1}{x^{3} - 9 x}=- \frac{20}{9 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{8}{9 \left(x - 3\right)} + \frac{1}{9 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- 3 x^{2} + 4 x - 1}{x^{3} - 9 x}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{9} - \frac{8 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{9} - \frac{20 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{9}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 6 x=x \left(x + 2\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{3 x^{2} - 4 x + 4}{x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 6 x}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x + 2} + \frac{C}{x}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=\frac{43}{3}$, $x=-2$ gives $B=-12$, $x=0$ gives $C=\frac{2}{3}$. So

\[\frac{3 x^{2} - 4 x + 4}{x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 6 x}=\frac{43}{3 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{12}{x + 2} + \frac{2}{3 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 x^{2} - 4 x + 4}{x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 6 x}\,dx=\frac{2 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{3} - 12 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)} + \frac{43 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{3}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} + x - 6}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} + x - 6=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} + x - 6}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=- \frac{9}{5}$, $x=2$ gives $B=- \frac{1}{5}$. So

\[\frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} + x - 6}=- \frac{9}{5 \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{1}{5 \left(x - 2\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 - 2 x}{x^{2} + x - 6}\,dx=- \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{5} - \frac{9 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{5}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4=\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{3 x^{2} - 4 x + 2}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x + 1} + \frac{C}{x - 2}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=\frac{11}{2}$, $x=-1$ gives $B=-3$, $x=2$ gives $C=\frac{1}{2}$. So

\[\frac{3 x^{2} - 4 x + 2}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4}=\frac{11}{2 \left(x + 2\right)} - \frac{3}{x + 1} + \frac{1}{2 \left(x - 2\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{3 x^{2} - 4 x + 2}{x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}}{2} - 3 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)} + \frac{11 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}}{2}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{4}{x^{2} - 3 x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 3 x=x \left(x - 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{4}{x^{2} - 3 x}=\frac{A}{x} + \frac{B}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=0$ gives $A=- \frac{4}{3}$, $x=3$ gives $B=\frac{4}{3}$. So

\[\frac{4}{x^{2} - 3 x}=\frac{4}{3 \left(x - 3\right)} - \frac{4}{3 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{4}{x^{2} - 3 x}\,dx=- \frac{4 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{3} + \frac{4 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{3}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 6 x=x \left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- x^{2} - 2 x - 4}{x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 6 x}=\frac{A}{x} + \frac{B}{x - 2} + \frac{C}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=0$ gives $A=- \frac{2}{3}$, $x=2$ gives $B=6$, $x=3$ gives $C=- \frac{19}{3}$. So

\[\frac{- x^{2} - 2 x - 4}{x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 6 x}=\frac{6}{x - 2} - \frac{19}{3 \left(x - 3\right)} - \frac{2}{3 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- x^{2} - 2 x - 4}{x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 6 x}\,dx=- \frac{2 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{3} - \frac{19 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{3} + 6 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int - \frac{1}{x^{2} - 2 x - 3}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 2 x - 3=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 1\right)$. Write

\[- \frac{1}{x^{2} - 2 x - 3}=\frac{A}{x + 1} + \frac{B}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-1$ gives $A=\frac{1}{4}$, $x=3$ gives $B=- \frac{1}{4}$. So

\[- \frac{1}{x^{2} - 2 x - 3}=\frac{1}{4 \left(x + 1\right)} - \frac{1}{4 \left(x - 3\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int - \frac{1}{x^{2} - 2 x - 3}\,dx=- \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{4} + \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)}}{4}+C.\]

Factor the denominator: $x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 2 x=x \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- 4 x^{2} + 4 x + 1}{x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 2 x}=\frac{A}{x + 2} + \frac{B}{x + 1} + \frac{C}{x}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-2$ gives $A=- \frac{23}{2}$, $x=-1$ gives $B=7$, $x=0$ gives $C=\frac{1}{2}$. So

\[\frac{- 4 x^{2} + 4 x + 1}{x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 2 x}=- \frac{23}{2 \left(x + 2\right)} + \frac{7}{x + 1} + \frac{1}{2 x}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- 4 x^{2} + 4 x + 1}{x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 2 x}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}}{2} + 7 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 1}\right| \right)} - \frac{23 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 2}\right| \right)}}{2}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{- 2 x - 2}{x^{2} + 2 x - 3}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} + 2 x - 3=\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{- 2 x - 2}{x^{2} + 2 x - 3}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x - 1}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=-1$, $x=1$ gives $B=-1$. So

\[\frac{- 2 x - 2}{x^{2} + 2 x - 3}=- \frac{1}{x + 3} - \frac{1}{x - 1}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{- 2 x - 2}{x^{2} + 2 x - 3}\,dx=- \ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)} - \ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{x}{x^{2} - 9}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 9=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)$. Write

\[\frac{x}{x^{2} - 9}=\frac{A}{x + 3} + \frac{B}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=-3$ gives $A=\frac{1}{2}$, $x=3$ gives $B=\frac{1}{2}$. So

\[\frac{x}{x^{2} - 9}=\frac{1}{2 \left(x + 3\right)} + \frac{1}{2 \left(x - 3\right)}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{x}{x^{2} - 9}\,dx=\frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{2} + \frac{\ln{\left(\left|{x + 3}\right| \right)}}{2}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \frac{4 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 4 x + 3}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Factor the denominator: $x^{2} - 4 x + 3=\left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 1\right)$. Write

\[\frac{4 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 4 x + 3}=\frac{A}{x - 1} + \frac{B}{x - 3}.\]

Multiply through by the denominator and plug in each root: $x=1$ gives $A=-1$, $x=3$ gives $B=-1$. So

\[\frac{4 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 4 x + 3}=- \frac{1}{x - 1} - \frac{1}{x - 3}.\]

Integrate each term:

\[\int \frac{4 - 2 x}{x^{2} - 4 x + 3}\,dx=- \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)} - \ln{\left(\left|{x - 1}\right| \right)}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \tan^{2}{\left(2 x \right)} \sec^{4}{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Save $\sec^22 x$ and write the other $\sec^2=1+\tan^2$. With $w=\tan 2 x$, $dw=2\sec^22 x\,dx$:

\[\int \tan^{2}{\left(2 x \right)} \sec^{4}{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{1}{2}\int \left(w^{4} + w^{2}\right)dw=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{w^{5}}{5} + \frac{w^{3}}{3}\right)+C.\]

Substituting back:

\[\int \tan^{2}{\left(2 x \right)} \sec^{4}{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{\tan^{5}{\left(2 x \right)}}{10} + \frac{\tan^{3}{\left(2 x \right)}}{6}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \sin^{4}{\left(2 x \right)} \cos^{5}{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
The power of $\cos$ is odd: save one $\cos 2 x$ and rewrite the rest with $\cos^2=1-\sin^2$. With $w=\sin 2 x$, $dw=2\cos 2 x\,dx$:

\[\int \sin^{4}{\left(2 x \right)} \cos^{5}{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{1}{2}\int \left(w^{8} - 2 w^{6} + w^{4}\right)dw=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{w^{9}}{9} - \frac{2 w^{7}}{7} + \frac{w^{5}}{5}\right)+C.\]

Substituting back:

\[\int \sin^{4}{\left(2 x \right)} \cos^{5}{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=\frac{\sin^{9}{\left(2 x \right)}}{18} - \frac{\sin^{7}{\left(2 x \right)}}{7} + \frac{\sin^{5}{\left(2 x \right)}}{10}+C.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int \sin^{5}{\left(x \right)} \cos^{4}{\left(x \right)}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
The power of $\sin$ is odd: save one $\sin x$ and rewrite the rest with $\sin^2=1-\cos^2$. With $w=\cos x$, $dw=-\sin x\,dx$:

\[\int \sin^{5}{\left(x \right)} \cos^{4}{\left(x \right)}\,dx=-\int \left(w^{8} - 2 w^{6} + w^{4}\right)dw=-\left(\frac{w^{9}}{9} - \frac{2 w^{7}}{7} + \frac{w^{5}}{5}\right)+C.\]

Substituting back:

\[\int \sin^{5}{\left(x \right)} \cos^{4}{\left(x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{\cos^{9}{\left(x \right)}}{9} + \frac{2 \cos^{7}{\left(x \right)}}{7} - \frac{\cos^{5}{\left(x \right)}}{5}+C.\]

Substituting back:

\[\int \sin^{3}{\left(x \right)}\,dx=\frac{\cos^{3}{\left(x \right)}}{3} - \cos{\left(x \right)}+C.\]

Substituting back:

\[\int \sec^{4}{\left(x \right)}\,dx=\frac{\tan^{3}{\left(x \right)}}{3} + \tan{\left(x \right)}+C.\]

The power of $\cos$ is odd: save one $\cos 2 x$ and rewrite the rest with $\cos^2=1-\sin^2$. With $w=\sin 2 x$, $dw=2\cos 2 x\,dx$:

Substituting back:

\[\int \cos^{3}{\left(2 x \right)}\,dx=- \frac{\sin^{3}{\left(2 x \right)}}{6} + \frac{\sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}+C.\]

\[\int_0^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Substitute $x=1\sin\theta,\quad dx=1\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{1-x^2}=1\cos\theta$. The limits $x=0$ and $x=\frac{1}{2}$ become $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}$:

\[\int_0^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\,dx=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,d\theta.\]

Use $\sin^2\theta=\frac{1-\cos2\theta}{2}$.

\[=\left[\frac{\theta}{2} - \frac{\sin{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}{2}\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}=- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8} + \frac{\pi}{12}.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int_0^{2 \sqrt{2}}\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Substitute $x=4\sin\theta,\quad dx=4\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{16-x^2}=4\cos\theta$. The limits $x=0$ and $x=2 \sqrt{2}$ become $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$:

\[\int_0^{2 \sqrt{2}}\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}\,dx=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}16 \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,d\theta.\]

Use $\cos^2\theta=\frac{1+\cos2\theta}{2}$.

\[=\left[8 \theta + 8 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}=4 + 2 \pi.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int_0^{4}\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Substitute $x=4\sin\theta,\quad dx=4\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{16-x^2}=4\cos\theta$. The limits $x=0$ and $x=4$ become $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$:

\[\int_0^{4}\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}\,dx=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}16 \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,d\theta.\]

Use $\cos^2\theta=\frac{1+\cos2\theta}{2}$.

\[=\left[8 \theta + 8 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}=4 \pi.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int_0^{\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{2}}\frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Substitute $x=3\sin\theta,\quad dx=3\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{9-x^2}=3\cos\theta$. The limits $x=0$ and $x=\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{2}$ become $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$:

\[\int_0^{\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{2}}\frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,dx=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}9 \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,d\theta.\]

Use $\sin^2\theta=\frac{1-\cos2\theta}{2}$.

\[=\left[\frac{9 \theta}{2} - \frac{9 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}{2}\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}=- \frac{9}{4} + \frac{9 \pi}{8}.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int_0^{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Substitute $x=2\sin\theta,\quad dx=2\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{4-x^2}=2\cos\theta$. The limits $x=0$ and $x=\sqrt{3}$ become $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$:

\[\int_0^{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}\,dx=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{3}}4 \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,d\theta.\]

Use $\cos^2\theta=\frac{1+\cos2\theta}{2}$.

\[=\left[2 \theta + 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{2 \pi}{3}.\]

variants.problem:

\[\int_0^{\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}}\frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,dx.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int_0^{3}\frac{1}{\left(x^{2} + 9\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Substitute $x=3\tan\theta,\quad dx=3\sec^2\theta\,d\theta,\quad (9+x^2)^{3/2}=27\sec^3\theta$. The limits $x=0$ and $x=3$ become $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$:

\[\int_0^{3}\frac{1}{\left(x^{2} + 9\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\,dx=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\frac{\cos{\left(\theta \right)}}{9}\,d\theta.\]\[=\left[\frac{\sin{\left(\theta \right)}}{9}\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{18}.\]

Use $\sin^2\theta=\frac{1-\cos2\theta}{2}$.

\[=\left[\frac{\theta}{2} - \frac{\sin{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}{2}\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}=- \frac{1}{4} + \frac{\pi}{8}.\]

variants.problem:
Evaluate

\[\int_{12}^{15}x \sqrt{16 - x}\,dx.\]

Evaluate

\[\int_{1}^{9}2 x \sqrt{10 - x}\,dx.\]

Evaluate

\[\int_{0}^{3}x \sqrt{4 - x}\,dx.\]
variants.solution:
Let $u=4-x$, so $x=4-u$ and $dx=-du$. When $x=0$, $u=4$; when $x=3$, $u=1$:

\[\int_{0}^{3}x \sqrt{4 - x}\,dx=-\int_{4}^{1}\sqrt{u} \left(4 - u\right)\,du=\int_{1}^{4}\left(- u^{\frac{3}{2}} + 4 \sqrt{u}\right)du=\left[- \frac{2 u^{\frac{5}{2}}}{5} + \frac{8 u^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}\right]_{1}^{4}=\frac{94}{15}.\]

templates.title: Volume of a solid with known cross-sections

variants.problem: The base of a solid is the region between $y=1-x^2$ and the $x$-axis. Cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are squares. Find the volume.
variants.solution:
At $x$ the section runs from $y=0$ up to $y=1 - x^{2}$, so the side length is $s=1 - x^{2}$ and the cross-section area is $A(x)=s^2$ with that $s$.

\[V=\int_{-1}^{1}A(x)\,dx=\int_{-1}^{1}\left(x^{4} - 2 x^{2} + 1\right)dx=\frac{16}{15}.\]

variants.problem: The base of a solid is the region between $y=4-x^2$ and the $x$-axis. Cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are equilateral triangles. Find the volume.
variants.solution:
At $x$ the section runs from $y=0$ up to $y=4 - x^{2}$, so the side length is $s=4 - x^{2}$ and the cross-section area is $A(x)=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2$ with that $s$.

\[V=\int_{-2}^{2}A(x)\,dx=\int_{-2}^{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x^{4}}{4} - 2 \sqrt{3} x^{2} + 4 \sqrt{3}\right)dx=\frac{128 \sqrt{3}}{15}.\]

variants.problem: The base of a solid is the region between $y=1-x^2$ and the $x$-axis. Cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are equilateral triangles. Find the volume.
variants.solution:
At $x$ the section runs from $y=0$ up to $y=1 - x^{2}$, so the side length is $s=1 - x^{2}$ and the cross-section area is $A(x)=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2$ with that $s$.

\[V=\int_{-1}^{1}A(x)\,dx=\int_{-1}^{1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x^{4}}{4} - \frac{\sqrt{3} x^{2}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)dx=\frac{4 \sqrt{3}}{15}.\]

variants.problem: The base of a solid is the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are squares. Find the volume.
variants.solution:
At $x$ the section runs from $y=0$ up to the line $y=1 - x$, so the side length is $s=1 - x$ and the cross-section area is $A(x)=s^2$ with that $s$.

\[V=\int_{0}^{1}A(x)\,dx=\int_{0}^{1}\left(x^{2} - 2 x + 1\right)dx=\frac{1}{3}.\]

variants.problem: The base of a solid is the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2,0)$ and $(0,3)$. Cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are squares. Find the volume.
variants.solution:
At $x$ the section runs from $y=0$ up to the line $y=3 - \frac{3 x}{2}$, so the side length is $s=3 - \frac{3 x}{2}$ and the cross-section area is $A(x)=s^2$ with that $s$.

\[V=\int_{0}^{2}A(x)\,dx=\int_{0}^{2}\left(\frac{9 x^{2}}{4} - 9 x + 9\right)dx=6.\]

templates.title: Volume of revolution by cylindrical shells

variants.problem: The region between $y=- x^{2} + 3 x$ and $y=2 x$ is rotated about the $y$-axis. Find the volume of the solid.
variants.solution:
The curves meet where $- x^{2} + 3 x=2 x$: $x=0$ and $x=1$. On $[0,1]$, $y=- x^{2} + 3 x$ is on top, so a shell at $x$ has height $- x^{2} + x$ and radius $x$ (its distance from the $y$-axis).

\[V=\int_0^{1}2\pi\left(x\right)\left(- x^{2} + x\right)dx=2\pi\int_0^{1}\left(- x^{3} + x^{2}\right)dx=\frac{\pi}{6}.\]

variants.problem: A cylindrical tank of radius $3$ ft and height $6$ ft holds water to a depth of $4$ ft. How much work does it take to pump all of the water over the top? (Use water weighs $62.5$ lb/ft³.)
variants.solution:
Measure $y$ up from the bottom. A thin slice at height $y$ has volume $\pi\left(3\right)^2dy$, so it weighs $\frac{125}{2}\pi\left(3\right)^2dy$, and it must be lifted $6 - y$ ft.

\[W=\int_0^{4}\frac{125}{2}\cdot 9 \pi\left(6 - y\right)dy=9000 \pi\approx 28,274\ \text{ft·lb}.\]

templates.title: The centroid of a region under a curve

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=9 - x^{2}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le3$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{0}^{3}9 - x^{2}\,dx=18$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{0}^{3}x \left(9 - x^{2}\right)\,dx=\frac{81}{4},\qquad \int_{0}^{3}\frac12\left(9 - x^{2}\right)^2dx=\frac{324}{5}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{\frac{81}{4}}{18}=\frac{9}{8},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{324}{5}}{18}=\frac{18}{5}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=\sin{\left(x \right)}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le\pi$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{0}^{\pi}\sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx=2$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{0}^{\pi}x \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx=\pi,\qquad \int_{0}^{\pi}\frac12\left(\sin{\left(x \right)}\right)^2dx=\frac{\pi}{4}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{\pi}{4}}{2}=\frac{\pi}{8}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=\frac{2}{x^{3}}$ and above the $x$-axis for $1\le x\le2$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{1}^{2}\frac{2}{x^{3}}\,dx=\frac{3}{4}$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{1}^{2}\frac{2}{x^{2}}\,dx=1,\qquad \int_{1}^{2}\frac12\left(\frac{2}{x^{3}}\right)^2dx=\frac{31}{80}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{1}{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{4}{3},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{31}{80}}{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{31}{60}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=\sqrt{x}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le4$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{0}^{4}\sqrt{x}\,dx=\frac{16}{3}$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{0}^{4}x^{\frac{3}{2}}\,dx=\frac{64}{5},\qquad \int_{0}^{4}\frac12\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^2dx=4.\]\[\bar x=\frac{\frac{64}{5}}{\frac{16}{3}}=\frac{12}{5},\qquad \bar y=\frac{4}{\frac{16}{3}}=\frac{3}{4}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=x^{3}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le1$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{0}^{1}x^{3}\,dx=\frac{1}{4}$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{0}^{1}x^{4}\,dx=\frac{1}{5},\qquad \int_{0}^{1}\frac12\left(x^{3}\right)^2dx=\frac{1}{14}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{\frac{1}{5}}{\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{4}{5},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{1}{14}}{\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{2}{7}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=x^{2}$ and above the $x$-axis for $1\le x\le3$.
variants.solution:

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{1}^{3}x^{3}\,dx=20,\qquad \int_{1}^{3}\frac12\left(x^{2}\right)^2dx=\frac{121}{5}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{20}{\frac{26}{3}}=\frac{30}{13},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{121}{5}}{\frac{26}{3}}=\frac{363}{130}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=e^{x}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le1$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{0}^{1}e^{x}\,dx=-1 + e$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{0}^{1}x e^{x}\,dx=1,\qquad \int_{0}^{1}\frac12\left(e^{x}\right)^2dx=- \frac{1}{4} + \frac{e^{2}}{4}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{1}{-1 + e}=\frac{1}{-1 + e},\qquad \bar y=\frac{- \frac{1}{4} + \frac{e^{2}}{4}}{-1 + e}=\frac{1}{4} + \frac{e}{4}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=4 - x^{2}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le2$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{0}^{2}4 - x^{2}\,dx=\frac{16}{3}$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{0}^{2}x \left(4 - x^{2}\right)\,dx=4,\qquad \int_{0}^{2}\frac12\left(4 - x^{2}\right)^2dx=\frac{128}{15}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{4}{\frac{16}{3}}=\frac{3}{4},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{128}{15}}{\frac{16}{3}}=\frac{8}{5}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=\sqrt{x}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le1$.
variants.solution:

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{0}^{1}x^{\frac{3}{2}}\,dx=\frac{2}{5},\qquad \int_{0}^{1}\frac12\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^2dx=\frac{1}{4}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{\frac{2}{5}}{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{3}{5},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{1}{4}}{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{3}{8}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=e^{x}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le2$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{0}^{2}e^{x}\,dx=-1 + e^{2}$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{0}^{2}x e^{x}\,dx=1 + e^{2},\qquad \int_{0}^{2}\frac12\left(e^{x}\right)^2dx=- \frac{1}{4} + \frac{e^{4}}{4}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{1 + e^{2}}{-1 + e^{2}}=\frac{1}{\tanh{\left(1 \right)}},\qquad \bar y=\frac{- \frac{1}{4} + \frac{e^{4}}{4}}{-1 + e^{2}}=\frac{1}{4} + \frac{e^{2}}{4}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=\frac{4}{x^{3}}$ and above the $x$-axis for $1\le x\le3$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{1}^{3}\frac{4}{x^{2}}\,dx=\frac{8}{3},\qquad \int_{1}^{3}\frac12\left(\frac{4}{x^{3}}\right)^2dx=\frac{1936}{1215}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{\frac{8}{3}}{\frac{16}{9}}=\frac{3}{2},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{1936}{1215}}{\frac{16}{9}}=\frac{121}{135}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=e^{x}$ and above the $x$-axis for $-1\le x\le1$.
variants.solution:
Area: $A=\int_{-1}^{1}e^{x}\,dx=e - e^{-1}$.

$\bar x=\dfrac1A\int x\,f(x)\,dx$ and $\bar y=\dfrac1A\int\frac12 f(x)^2\,dx$:

\[\int_{-1}^{1}x e^{x}\,dx=\frac{2}{e},\qquad \int_{-1}^{1}\frac12\left(e^{x}\right)^2dx=- \frac{1}{4 e^{2}} + \frac{e^{2}}{4}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{\frac{2}{e}}{e - e^{-1}}=- \frac{2}{1 - e^{2}},\qquad \bar y=\frac{- \frac{1}{4 e^{2}} + \frac{e^{2}}{4}}{e - e^{-1}}=\frac{\cosh{\left(1 \right)}}{2}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=x^{2}$ and above the $x$-axis for $1\le x\le2$.

\[\int_{1}^{2}x^{3}\,dx=\frac{15}{4},\qquad \int_{1}^{2}\frac12\left(x^{2}\right)^2dx=\frac{31}{10}.\]\[\bar x=\frac{\frac{15}{4}}{\frac{7}{3}}=\frac{45}{28},\qquad \bar y=\frac{\frac{31}{10}}{\frac{7}{3}}=\frac{93}{70}.\]

variants.problem: Find the centroid of the region under $y=2 \sin{\left(x \right)}$ and above the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le\pi$.
